extracted.intended_audience: Registered and prospective practitioners (attorneys and agents) who appear or seek to appear before the United States Patent and Trademark Office; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff; law firms advising practitioners on USPTO conduct rules.
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed amendments to 37 CFR Parts 1, 2, 7, 11, and 41 establishing definitions, practitioner obligations, disciplinary jurisdiction and procedures, recordkeeping and certification rules for persons practicing before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct: conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 11.804(i) would clearly set forth that it continues to be misconduct for a practitioner to engage in conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner’s fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes conduct that leads to public discipline by any duly constituted authority of a State, the United States, or the country in which the practitioner resides (see 37 CFR 11.24). Violations may lead to disciplinary proceedings under Part 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary jurisdiction and authority of the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The disciplinary jurisdiction of the Office is set forth in section 11.19. The USPTO Director has statutory (35 U.S.C. 2(b)(2)(D) and 32) and inherent authority to adopt rules regulating the practice of attorneys and other persons before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and non-patent law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have affirmed that agencies have inherent power to discipline professionals who practice before them (cited cases: Goldsmith v. U.S. Board of Tax Appeals; Herman v. Dulles; Koden v. U.S. Dep't of Justice; Polydoroff v. ICC; Touche Ross & Co. v. SEC). The USPTO is declining to adopt the ABA Model Rule regarding disciplinary authority and choice of law, but asserts its own rulemaking and disciplinary authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Savings clauses for disciplinary proceedings (§11.901)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 11.901 would contain the following savings clauses: (a) A disciplinary proceeding based on conduct engaged in prior to the effective date of these regulations may be instituted subsequent to such effective date, if such conduct would continue to justify disciplinary sanctions under the provisions of this part; (b) No practitioner shall be subject to a disciplinary proceeding under this part based on conduct engaged in before the effective date hereof if such conduct would not have been subject to disciplinary action before such effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves ability to pursue discipline for pre-effective-date misconduct that remains sanctionable, and protects practitioners from retroactive application to conduct that was not sanctionable prior to the rules' effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications under §11.18: presentation as certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1.4(d)(4)(i): The presentation to the Office (whether by signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating) of any paper by a party, whether a practitioner or non-practitioner, constitutes a certification under § 11.18(b) of this subchapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of §11.18(b)(2) by any party may result in sanctions under §11.18(c); any practitioner violating §11.18(b) may also be subject to disciplinary action (see §11.18(d)). This ties ordinary filings to explicit certification/verification obligations and potential sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with ABA Model Rules (Table 1 principal-source mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1 lists the principal source of sections 11.101 through 11.804 (e.g., §11.101 — MRPC 1.1; §11.102 — MRPC 1.2; many sections mapped to MRPC rules; some sections designated 'USPTO' or other sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates proposed rules are largely drawn from the ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct (MRPC) with USPTO-specific adaptations; consult the Table for the specific MRPC source tied to each §11 provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner records maintenance and disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules will require that registered practitioners and attorneys who appear before the Office maintain complete records of clients, including all funds, securities and other properties of clients coming into his/her possession, and render appropriate accounts to the client regarding such records, as well as report violations of the rules to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record keeping and maintenance are considered usual and customary for practitioners and for many attorneys will align with state bar requirements; compliance with the practitioner's state rules (for attorneys employed in the U.S.) will be deemed compliance with the Office’s requirements in certain respects (see §11.115(f)(4) and (f)(5)). Records must allow cooperation with investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent: definition and confirmation in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Informed consent means the agreement by a person to a proposed course of conduct after the practitioner has communicated adequate information and explanation about the material risks of and reasonably available alternatives to the proposed course of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirmed in writing, when used in reference to the informed consent of a person, means informed consent given in writing or a writing a practitioner promptly transmits to the person confirming oral informed consent; if not feasible at the time consent is given, the practitioner must obtain or transmit the writing within a reasonable time thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud / fraudulent: definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraud or fraudulent means conduct that involves a misrepresentation of material fact made with intent to deceive or a state of mind so reckless respecting consequences as to be the equivalent of intent, where there is justifiable reliance on the misrepresentation by the party deceived, inducing the party to act thereon, and where there is injury to the party deceived resulting from reliance on the misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fraud may also be established by purposeful omission or failure to state a material fact which makes other statements misleading, provided justifiable reliance and resulting injury are shown. This definition supplies the elements the Office will consider when evaluating alleged fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law-related services: scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Law-related services means services that might reasonably be performed in conjunction with and in substance are related to the provision of legal services, and that are not prohibited as unauthorized practice of law when provided by a non-lawyer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that non-lawyers may perform certain law-related services if not prohibited as unauthorized practice of law; useful for determining who is subject to practitioner rules versus allowed non-lawyer activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner: who qualifies
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner means: (1) An attorney or agent registered to practice before the Office in patent matters; (2) An individual authorized under 5 U.S.C. 500(b) or otherwise as provided by §11.14(a),(b),(c) to practice before the Office in trademark matters or other non-patent matters; (3) An individual authorized to practice before the Office in a patent case or matters under §11.9(a) or (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the classes of persons subject to Part 11 obligations (attorneys, agents, and certain authorized individuals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable belief and 'reasonably believes' standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable belief or reasonably believes when used in reference to a practitioner means that the practitioner believes the matter in question and that the circumstances are such that the belief is reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets an objective-reasonableness overlay on the practitioner's subjective belief for compliance and disciplinary assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably should know standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonably should know when used in reference to a practitioner means that a practitioner of reasonable prudence and competence would ascertain the matter in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a negligence/knowledge standard applicable in assessing practitioner obligations and potential discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screened: isolation procedures for conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Screened means the isolation of a practitioner from any participation in a matter through the timely imposition of procedures within a firm that are reasonably adequate under the circumstances to protect information that the isolated practitioner is obligated to protect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable form of ethical screen: timely, firm-level procedures reasonably adequate to protect confidential information; relevant where disqualification or conflict screening is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribunal: definition of adjudicative body
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribunal means the Office, a court, an arbitrator in a binding arbitration proceeding or a legislative body, administrative agency or other body acting in an adjudicative capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A body acts in adjudicative capacity when a neutral official, after presentation of evidence or legal argument by a party, will render a binding legal judgment directly affecting a party’s interests in a particular matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing or written: inclusive definition and electronic signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing or written means a tangible or electronic record of a communication or representation, including handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photography, audio or video recording and email. A 'signed' writing includes an electronic sound, symbol or process attached to or logically associated with a writing and executed or adopted by a person with the intent to sign the writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirms that electronic records and e-signatures satisfy 'writing' requirements for practitioner obligations and notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to OED Director regarding enrollment or recognition (timing and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition from any action or requirement of the staff of OED reporting to the OED Director shall be taken to the OED Director accompanied by payment of the fee set forth in §1.21(a)(5)(i). Any such petition not filed within sixty days from the mailing date of the action or notice from which relief is requested will be dismissed as untimely. The filing of a petition will neither stay the period for taking other action which may be running, nor stay other proceedings. The petitioner may file a single request for reconsideration of a decision within thirty days of the date of the decision. Filing a request for reconsideration stays the period for seeking review of the OED Director’s decision until a final decision on the request for reconsideration is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets concrete timeliness (60 days for initial petitions to OED Director, 30 days for single reconsideration) and clarifies non-stay effect of petition filing on other time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of OED Director’s decision by USPTO Director (timing, record, and evidence limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with a final decision of the OED Director regarding enrollment or recognition shall seek review upon petition to the USPTO Director accompanied by payment of fee (§1.21(a)(5)(ii)). By filing such petition the party waives any right to seek reconsideration from the OED Director. Any petition not filed within thirty days after the final decision of the OED Director may be dismissed as untimely. Briefs or memoranda, if any, shall accompany the petition. The petition will be decided on the basis of the record made before the OED Director. The USPTO Director in deciding the petition will consider no new evidence. Copies of documents already of record shall not be submitted. An oral hearing will not be granted except when considered necessary by the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that USPTO Director review is limited to the existing record (no new evidence) and short timeliness; briefs permitted but no automatic oral hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions in disciplinary matters to USPTO Director (content and proof requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with any action or notice of any employee of the OED during or at the conclusion of a disciplinary investigation shall seek review upon petition to the OED Director; a party dissatisfied with the OED Director’s final decision shall seek review upon petition to the USPTO Director. Any petition must contain a statement of the facts involved and the point(s) to be reviewed and the action requested. Briefs or memoranda, if any, in support must accompany the petition. Where facts are to be proven, the proof in the form of affidavits or declarations (and exhibits, if any) must accompany the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED Director may be directed to file a reply; oral hearing to USPTO Director only when necessary; filing a petition will not stay investigations or proceedings; petitions not filed within thirty days of mailing of the underlying action/notice may be dismissed as untimely; only a USPTO Director decision denying a petition constitutes a final decision for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information maintenance requirement (§11.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered practitioner must notify the OED Director of his or her postal address for office, up to three email addresses where he or she receives email, and business telephone number, as well as every change to any of said addresses or telephone numbers within thirty days of the date of the change. A registered practitioner shall separately file written notice of change of address or telephone number to the OED Director. An attorney in good standing shall provide the OED Director with the State bar identification number associated with each membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director will publish a roster containing name, postal business addresses, business telephone number, registration number, and registration status for each registered practitioner recognized to practice before the Office in patent cases. Failure to respond to OED inquiries may trigger administrative suspension procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative suspension procedure for noncompliance with notice/fee requirements (§11.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If it appears a registered practitioner has failed to comply with contact/fee requirements, OED Director shall publish and send a notice demanding compliance and payment of a delinquency fee within sixty days. Failure to comply leads to a Rule to Show Cause; the practitioner may file a response within 30 days to the USPTO Director; OED may file a reply within 10 days. If USPTO Director finds no genuine issues of material fact regarding notice or failure to pay fees, the USPTO Director shall enter an order administratively suspending the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An administratively suspended practitioner is prohibited from practicing before the Office in patent cases while suspended, remains subject to investigation and discipline for conduct before/during/after suspension, and may be disciplined for practicing while suspended. The Rule to Show Cause is filed and processed with specified timing; filing does not stay other proceedings.
